items.name: Backfill is safe to run twice
items.note: backfill-people.php --go inserted a fresh person for every group regardless of existing links, repointed every record at the duplicate and orphaned the original with its right-to-work checks, verifications, eligibility and leave records. Both the quickstart and the production runbook run it after a seed, when everything is already linked. It now leaves linked rows alone and gives an unlinked row its group's existing person; a group pointing at two different people is reported, never merged. items.name: Shifts, templates and recurrence
items.note: Creating was the whole of it: a shift could not be reassigned, taken off somebody or cancelled, so a worker falling ill left a wrong row on the rota with no route out but the database. scheduling.php now carries assign, unassign and cancel, each behind the same deployment gate and clash check as creating, and Scheduling opens a shift on click. has_clash() ignores archived shifts and the shift being moved, so a shift no longer clashes with itself. Template generation created shifts in the past: the weekday offset is 0 when today is the template's own weekday, so generating on a Monday afternoon produced that morning's 09:00 shift. Past occurrences are skipped, and the duplicate guard now respects deleted_at, which was silently blocking a slot's regeneration.

items.name: Work orders (jobs)
items.note: Care visits, cleans, guard shifts and courses on one spine. Untracked here until now, and it showed: a typo in a date was stored as 1970-01-01, an "Other" job was filed under Care whatever it was for, notes were collected and never shown, there was no edit and nothing ever set deleted_at. The status enum had "assigned" with no assignee column anywhere, so the status was decorative; migration 030 adds assigned_to and the assignment runs the same deployment gate as the rota, so the job board cannot name somebody a shift would refuse.

items.name: Smart matching on skills and availability
Shift broadcast with token acceptance
items.note: shift_offers, SMS link, no login required. Accepting now runs the gate; a refusal expires the offer, audits shift.blocked and notifies the office. Broadcast is rate-limited: each one sends a chargeable message per eligible worker and nothing stopped it being replayed.

items.name: Field events: clock in/out, check-in, panic, signature
items.note: shift_events with lat/lng. Location is personal data about the worker (docs/PRIVACY.md) and was gated by nothing: is_staff() is true for editor, trainer and employee, so a content role could read a named colleague's coordinates to six decimal places. Coordinates now need the 'employment' zone, or the trail being the caller's own. The board also dropped a shift the moment it was clocked out, and ran one query per shift for its events; both fixed. A panic alert still cannot be acknowledged and, separately, notifies nobody -- notifications.php forces every broadcast to read. A panic alert also reached nobody: it is a broadcast, and notifications had no per-user read state, so it arrived marked read and the bell never lit (migration 025). It can be acknowledged now (migration 026) instead of latching for the day, the clock sequence is validated, and check_in -- accepted by the API and advertised in the palette since the beginning -- can finally be sent from the worker app.

items.name: Timesheets and pay rules
items.note: Three defects found by exercising it. A shift crossing midnight was rejected outright, so a business running waking nights could not record one; the calculation is now rg_shift_minutes() in pure.php, UTC and tested. Reads were open to any internal account, so an editor could pull every worker's hours; every branch now takes the payroll zone, and src/lib/access.ts matches. A manager could only ever approve, never reject: migration 021 adds 'rejected', decided_at and decision_note, and a reason is required. The page defaults to the current month and filters by period and status. Two more found on a second pass: the approval tiles were summed in PHP over the fetched page, so past the page size the figure the office acts on was an under-count, and they are now aggregated by the database over the whole filter; and overtime reset at the pay-period boundary because the 40-hour threshold is weekly while the query was monthly, so a week straddling a month end was counted from zero twice. pay_compute() now scans whole ISO weeks and pays only the days inside the period. The arithmetic itself was untestable: base pay, the overtime split, the premium application and both roundings all lived inside pay_compute()'s result loop, which takes a mysqli. pay_entry() and pay_holiday() are pure and carry 21 assertions; pay_compute() calls them and its output is unchanged to the penny. A further pass on the money itself: pay rates had no history, so a rise re-priced every past period (migration 022); bank holidays stopped at 2026-12-28, so every 2027 one would have paid flat (migration 023, generated by a tested function); premiums were chosen for a whole entry from its start hour, so a 05:00-13:00 shift was paid night for all eight hours (rg_premium_segments); nothing checked a rate was plausible (migration 024, a dated floor, empty by default, flags not blocks); and the PDF was titled PAYSLIP while showing gross with no deductions and no net. Two structural gaps closed as well (migration 029): there was no unpaid break at all, so gross hours were paid door to door, and a timesheet had no link to the shift it was worked on, so the same shift could be claimed and paid twice with nothing showing it. Clock events still do not become timesheets automatically. me.php?action=payslip had also existed since the beginning with nothing calling it; the worker app shows it now, gross and labelled as such.

items.name: Marketing consent and unsubscribe
items.note: Optional unticked box on the contact and quote forms, marketing_allowed() where the latest consent_log row wins and no row means no, and unsubscribe.php reached from an email with no login, authenticated by an HMAC over the address. items.note: src/pages/app/Today.tsx at /app replaces the Command Centre: "Today, <weekday date>", tiles for unfilled shifts, checks to review, evidence expiring in 30 days and approvals waiting (left out when the account may not see them), today's shifts with state chips linking to the rota (office), and Needs action from action-centre.php with named people linking to their profiles. items.note: cqc_pack, sia_acs, coshh, skills_for_care. S5: now take the compliance zone and the service scope

items.name: Staff workload view

items.name: Audit log
items.note: Migration 009 adds entity_type, entity_id, before_json, after_json, reason, ip and user_agent, plus three indexes. audit() keeps its signature so all existing call sites work unchanged and gain IP and agent automatically

items.name: GDPR export and erasure
items.note: Export resolves through the people spine in both directions -- people.email is routinely empty when the row came from an application -- and returns 27 collections instead of 5, names what it leaves out, and is written to export_log. Erasure anonymises public-form data and routes everything else to the four-eyes deletion workflow instead of erasing immediately

items.name: Incidents with RIDDOR and safeguarding flags
Database backup with rotation
items.note: above the document root, 14-day prune

items.name: Restore testing
items.note: Reported as a WARN that cannot be inferred, rather than assumed to be fine. A backup nobody has restored is a hope, not a backup -- the check says so rather than staying silent

items.name: Retention engine
items.note: server/retention-sweep.php is the consumer retention_policies never had. Reports by default, acts only with --go from the CLI, acts only where a period is set, and never hard-deletes: review raises a task, archive sets deleted_at, delete opens a request in the approval workflow. All 14 periods are NULL, so it changes nothing until the business sets one

items.name: Deletion approval workflow
items.note: server/governance.php. Staff request with a reason of at least 10 characters; somebody else approves. Four eyes enforced: the approver may not be the requester. Archive is the default disposition

items.name: System health dashboard
items.note: server/system-health.php, shown in Settings, System health (S5). Live checks plus when each scheduled job last ran (cron_runs, migration 041: backup, expiry alerts, retention sweep, mail drainer) shown as ok, late or unknown, the email queue with recent failures (no recipients) and per-form intake health. The restore test stays an explicit unknown. Scoped accounts are refused. db case 220_system_health

items.name: Reconcile part-paid Direct Debit collections
items.note: Fixed. Credits the amount actually collected, marks paid only when it covers the total, and is idempotent against webhook redelivery

items.name: A record's own history is retrievable
items.note: audit.php?entity_type=worker&entity_id=12. Reading the log with a filter is itself audited, but the routine full listing is not, so the log does not fill with entries about reading the log

items.name: Integration failure surfaced
items.note: Silent integrations and unmappable submissions both reach the Action Centre

items.name: Deletion requires approval
items.note: Verified: an admin cannot approve their own request

items.name: Export data
items.note: Logged with user, scope, purpose, record count and IP

items.name: Archiving actually hides the record
items.note: Every list and count query for the newly soft-deletable tables filters on deleted_at. An archive that leaves the row visible is not an archive

items.name: Backups are restore-tested
items.note: Surfaced by system-health.php as an explicit unknown

items.name: Unapplied migrations are visible
items.note: A deploy that ships migration files without running them looks completely normal until something fails oddly. system-health.php compares the directory against schema_migrations

items.name: Data-subject request pathway
items.note: /data-request and server/data-request.php. Public form, reference, acknowledgement, staff queue with a status trail. Collects no identity documents and self-serves nothing -- whether a deletion can be honoured depends on employment and safeguarding duties a form cannot weigh. No statutory deadline is written into the code

items.name: Sensitive zones enforced
items.note: can_view_zone() existed and was called once, for payroll. Now enforced for compliance (workers.php, compliance.php) and health (leave.php, where a person always sees their own). disciplinary, legal and employment have no feature storing that data yet. The person profile (server/people.php) returns each section behind its zone -- compliance for checks, training and contracts, payroll for pay history, health for leave reasons, employment for emergency contacts -- as {restricted: true} rather than data

items.name: Privacy documentation
items.note: docs/PRIVACY.md is an evidence-backed data inventory with file:line provenance; docs/COOKIES.md is verified at runtime; docs/RETENTION.md carries the schedule with every period marked as needing legal review

items.name: Approved deletion removes the document itself
items.note: A hard delete used to remove the files row and leave the bytes on disk under a random name: gone from the system, still on the server, no longer findable. governance.php now unlinks it and audits it. Archive keeps the bytes, which is what makes it recoverable. Verified end to end against a local database

items.note: vite-plugin-pwa with a build-hash precache manifest, so a deploy invalidates exactly what changed and offline survives it

items.note: Owned by PwaStatus, which also owns the update prompt. Registering in main.tsx as well would race it

items.name: Cached read-only worker data
items.note: NetworkFirst on me.php and notifications.php with a 5-second timeout. The rest of the PHP API is never cached: stale compliance data would mean showing an eligibility answer that is no longer true

items.name: Update-available prompt
items.note: src/components/pwa-status.tsx, registerType 'prompt'. Never automatic: swapping the app out from under someone part-way through clocking in is its own failure

items.name: Offline banner
items.note: Says what still works, not just that something is wrong

items.name: Offline write queue
items.note: OUT OF SCOPE by decision, not outstanding. Writes require connectivity: a queued clock-in that turns out to be invalid when it lands is worse than being told plainly that you are offline

items.name: Install payload trimmed
items.note: 37 MB of orphaned Pulse-UI template assets removed (cards, products, illustrations, carousels, countries) -- shipped on every deploy and precached into the app. Precache 14.5 MB across 115 entries down to 1.15 MB across 67. The office-only chunks are excluded too: a field worker should not download a charts library, a calendar and a PDF engine

items.note: favicon.svg and the 192, 512, maskable and iOS touch PNGs redrawn in the company green (2026 design system); the PNGs are rendered from SVG with ImageMagick, as docs/DESIGN_SYSTEM.md describes

items.name: CI quality gates

items.note: Two dependency-free suites, both in CI: server/tests/run.php (466 assertions over pure server logic plus the endpoint-guard check in server/tests/guards.php) and src/lib/__tests__/access.test.ts (over the permission map). Endpoints and components are still untested end to end

items.note: Full detail goes to error_log with a reference; the caller gets the reference only, unless GK_DEBUG is on

items.note: 12 packages with zero imports removed, plus the dead editor chunk they were splitting into

items.name: ESLint baseline clean
items.note: 0 errors, from 33. The last 19 were cleared by changing the code, not the rules: the unreferenced src/components/calendar template deleted, effects in Scheduling/Verify/auth-provider/theme-toggle restructured so none sets state synchronously, icons rendered with createElement, homeFor/openStorageNotice/PageLoader moved out of component modules, sidebar skeleton width derived from useId. CI runs eslint --max-warnings 0 and blocks

items.name: Documentation consistency enforced in CI
items.note: scripts/docs_sync.py --check

items.name: Prepared statements in dashboard.php
items.note: Every division filter is bound. The value was already allowlisted so it was not injectable, but the guarantee depended on remembering that, and the next person adding a filter had a pattern to copy that did not carry it

items.name: Typecheck actually enforces the strict config
items.note: tsconfig.json had no references, so tsc -b built a root config lacking noUnusedLocals and tsconfig.app.json was orphaned. Now referenced, and the script uses --force so a warm cache cannot make the gate a no-op

items.name: Build artefacts out of version control
items.note: tsconfig.tsbuildinfo was tracked despite being gitignored; untracked, and both projects now write build info under node_modules/.tmp

items.name: Pure logic separated from the kernel
items.note: server/pure.php holds config-free, database-free domain logic so it can be tested directly. classify(), tier_for() and field_status() were duplicated definitions inside endpoint files; they now share one implementation

items.name: Failed queries no longer pass silently
items.note: lib.php set MYSQLI_REPORT_OFF and almost no call site checked execute(), so a failed INSERT was ignored and the endpoint reported success -- workers.php returned HTTP 200 with a complete worker object, id 0, for a row never written. Now MYSQLI_REPORT_ERROR|STRICT, set after the connection so config.php keeps its own message

items.name: Frontend types match the server
items.note: Person, EligibilityVerdict, RequirementState, RightToWorkCheck, AuditEntry, QueuedEmail added to src/lib/types.ts. A narrower duplicate AuditEntry was merged rather than left to drift

items.name: Reassessment can run without sending mail
items.note: expiry-alerts.php --reassess-only. Folding reassessment into the alerts cron made recalculating and emailing the workforce one action, so running it during a deployment sent real reminders to real people at a time nobody chose

items.name: Migration production guard is meaningful on cPanel
items.note: Was inferred from DB_HOST, and on cPanel the production database is localhost too — so the live system read as local: migrate.php --go skipped the typed-name confirmation, backfill-people.php --go wrote unchallenged, and seed.php --confirm --reset would have emptied clients, workers and invoices. Now declared as RG_ENV in config.php and read through rg_is_local_database(); a config.php without it is treated as production. Verified: with RG_ENV=production, seed and backfill refuse and migrate demands --production and the typed database name

items.name: No third-party requests from the public site
items.note: Google Fonts was the only one and sent every visitor's IP and user agent to Google on first paint. Self-hosted under public/fonts; both origins removed from the CSP and the service worker. Verified: a cold load requests nothing but the site's own origin

items.name: Design system: company green, Source Serif 4 headlines
items.note: src/index.css tokens and tailwind.config.ts rebuilt on #33512D with warm neutrals, status colours that are not the brand green, one 8px radius and a green-black dark mode. Source Serif 4 (500, 600) self-hosted for website headlines; Plus Jakarta Sans removed. Navy and mint retired. docs/DESIGN_SYSTEM.md rewritten. Website page designs are S6

items.name: Eight-destination office navigation

Published role pages and posts live in the database, which the build in CI cannot reach, so server/sitemap.php lists them (public, cached an hour, drafts and closed roles never listed). robots.txt names both. server/tests/db/cases/170_careers_cms.php

items.note: EmploymentAgency and LocalBusiness on the home page, Service on each service page, Article on news posts, JobPosting on role pages (S7: title, description, date posted, organisation, location; no salary because pay is optional free text), from src/lib/structured-data.ts. items.name: Forms directory and embedded Google Forms (S7, F23)
items.note: Migration 039 website_forms and server/website-forms.php. Only https://docs.google.com/forms/d/e/<id>/viewform is accepted (rg_parse_google_form(), 422 for anything else) and only the id is stored; the website builds the iframe from it (src/lib/google-forms.ts). The frame loads only after the visitor presses Load the application form from Google; Open the form in a new tab and the phone number are always shown. CSP gains frame-src https://docs.google.com only. Previous values are in the audit log and shown as history. Settings, Form intake lists forms not reviewed for 90 days and each one intake health. No sandbox attribute: submission inside a sandbox could not be tested without a real form

Instagram, Facebook, LinkedIn, TikTok and a WhatsApp enquiry link, each checked against its own host; X is not offered

items.note: Request staff, Arrange care, Current roles, Training, Contact, the office phone, then the social profiles and WhatsApp link from the company record. Text only, no third-party requests
